passages.original: et ideo tanquam ante conspectum Dei, ita in medio vestri fidem meam protuli conscius admodum sententiae divinae dicentis : Non celavi misericordiam tuam et veritatem tuam a congregatione multa : vel apostolum Paulum Thimoteo discipulo praecipientem audivi : Certa bonum certa- men fidei, apprehende vitam aeternam in qua vocatus es, et confessus bonam confessionem coram multis testi- bus : vera est enim Redemptoris nostri ex Evangelio sententia, qua confitentem se coram hominibus con- fiteri dicit, coram Patre, et negantem se esse negatu- rum. Expedit enim nobis id ore confiteri b quod corde credimus, secundum coeleste mandatum quo dicitur : Corde creditur ad justitiam, oris autem con- fessio fit ad salutem : proinde sicut anathematizo Arium omnibus dogmatibus et complicibus suis, qui unigenitum Dei Filium a paterna degenerem as- serebat esse substantia, nec a Patre genitum, sed ec nihilo dicebat esse creatum, vel omnia concilia mali- gnantium quae adversus sanctam synodum Nicaenam exstiterunt, ita in honorem et in laudem fidem san- ctam Nicaeni observo et honoro concilii, quam con- tra eumdem rectas fidei pestem Arium trecentorum decem et octo sancta episcopalis scripsit synodus;
passages.english: And therefore, as before the sight of God, so in your midst I have set forth my faith, being fully aware of the divine saying which says: "I have not concealed your mercy and your truth from the great congregation"; or I have heard the apostle Paul instructing his disciple Timothy: "Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold of eternal life, to which you were called, and you have confessed the good confession before many witnesses." For true is the saying of our Redeemer from the Gospel, in which he says that he will confess before the Father the one who confesses him before men, and will deny the one who denies him. For it is fitting for us to confess with the mouth what we believe in the heart, according to the heavenly command in which it is said: "With the heart one believes unto righteousness, but confession of the mouth is made unto salvation." Accordingly, just as I anathematize Arius with all his doctrines and his accomplices, who asserted that the only-begotten Son of God was degenerate from, [that is, unequal to,] the Father's substance, and said that he was not begotten from the Father but created out of nothing, and [I anathematize] all the councils of the malignant which arose against the holy synod of Nicaea, so, to its honour and praise, I observe and honour the holy faith of the council of Nicaea, which the holy episcopal synod of three hundred and eighteen wrote against that same plague of the right faith, Arius;
passages.notes: "ec nihilo" read as "ex nihilo"; "rectas fidei" read as "rectae fidei". Stray "b" after "confiteri" is a footnote mark. "a paterna degenerem ... substantia": literally "degenerate from the paternal substance", i.e. not of the same substance; bracketed gloss could be omitted.

passages.original: Denique coruscante sanctae operationis exemplo, partim desidia, partim consuetudine in quibusdam ecclesiis in Coenae Domini (??)tione pedes fratrum a sacerdotibus non lavantur, nihil allud obtendentes 592 nisi solam traditionis consuetudi- nem, cum Veritas objurgans dicat : Quare vot trans- gredimint mandatum Dei propter traditionem restrum? itemque praecellentissimus doctor et invictissimus martyr Cyprianus prosequens ait : Frustra qui ra- tione vincuntur consuetudinem nobis opponunt, quasi consuetudo major sit veritate, aut non id sit spiritualibus sequendum quod in melius fuerit a sancto Spiritu revelatum; ideoque dum veritatis exemplum luce clarius enitescat et objurgationis ejus terribilia edicta praefulgeant, atque etiam docto- ris praecipui sententia instruat majorem esse veri- tatem consuetudine, incussum nobis consuetudinem sine ratione objiciunt.
passages.english: Then, although the example of this holy action shines brightly, in some churches, partly through negligence and partly through custom, the feet of the brethren are not washed by the priests at the [celebration] of the Lord's Supper, and they put forward nothing other than the mere custom of tradition, although the Truth says in rebuke: "Why do you transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?" Likewise the most excellent teacher and most invincible martyr Cyprian, pursuing [the point], says: "In vain do those who are overcome by reason set custom against us, as if custom were greater than truth, or as if spiritual men ought not to follow what has been revealed for the better by the Holy Spirit." And so, while the example of the truth shines clearer than light, and the terrible decrees of its rebuke blaze forth, and the judgement of the outstanding teacher also teaches that truth is greater than custom, they persistently throw custom at us without reason.
passages.notes: The word before 'tione' is illegible in the scan; probably 'celebratione' or similar, rendered '[celebration]'. Scanning errors corrected: 'vot trans- gredimint' = 'vos transgredimini', 'restrum' = 'vestram'. 'incussum' is obscure, perhaps a corruption of 'incassum' ('in vain') or 'incessanter'; rendered 'persistently', but 'in vain they throw custom at us' is also possible.

passages.original: IV. Si quis Natalem Christi secundum carnem non vere honorat, sed honorare se simulat jejunans in eo- dem die, et in dominico, quia Christum in vera ho- minis natura natum esse non credidit, sicut Cerdon, Marcion, Manichaeus et Priscillianus dixerunt, ana- thema sit
passages.english: IV. If anyone does not truly honour the Nativity of Christ according to the flesh, but pretends to honour it while fasting on that same day and on the Lord's day, because he has not believed that Christ was born in the true nature of man, as Cerdo, Marcion, Manichaeus and Priscillian said, let him be anathema.

passages.original: Denique spiritus promptus, caro autem infirma; tristis est au- tem non ipse, sed anima, non est tristis sapientia, non divina substantia, sed anima : suscepit corpus meum, non me fefellit ut aliud esset et aliud videretur. Sanctus Athanasius in tractata quem scripsit de Christi Nativitate sie dicit : In hoc sit ergo, fratres charissimi, fides nostra, in hoc tota salus et vita con- sistat, ut credamus Deam Dei Filium primum ante omnia saecula a Deo Patre invisibiliter et impassibili- ter genitum, deinde ex Maria virgine secundum ho- minem natum, ei secundum hunc hominem passum, mortuum et sepultum resurrexisse, ab inferis ascen- disse in coelum.
passages.english: Then, "the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak"; and it is not he himself who is sorrowful, but the soul. Wisdom is not sorrowful, the divine substance is not, but the soul: "He took up my body; he did not deceive me, so that he was one thing and seemed another." Saint Athanasius, in the treatise which he wrote on the Nativity of Christ, speaks thus: "Let our faith, then, dearest brethren, rest in this, let our whole salvation and life consist in this: that we believe that God the Son of God was first, before all ages, begotten of God the Father invisibly and impassibly; then was born of the Virgin Mary according to [his] humanity; and that, having suffered, died and been buried according to this humanity, he rose again and ascended from the underworld into heaven."
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'tractata' = 'tractatu', 'sie' = 'sic', 'Deam' = 'Deum', 'ei' = 'et'. The phrase 'suscepit corpus meum ... videretur' appears to be quoted from the patristic source, but its subject is unclear, and the boundaries of the quotation are uncertain.
